# Graphics3D

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [Display](Blitz3D-Display)

</div>


```blitzbasic
Graphics3D width:Int32, height:Int32, depth:Int32=0, mode:Int32=0
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `width` | Int32 | required | Width of the picture in pixels. |
| `height` | Int32 | required | Height of the picture in pixels. |
| `depth` | Int32 | `0` | Color depth, which picks the format of the buffers: 24 for R8G8B8X8, 30 for R10G10B10A2, 32 for R8G8B8A8 and 64 for R16G16B16A16 (half precision floats, never integers). 0 gives 32. Defaults to 0. |
| `mode` | Int32 | `0` | Window or full screen as in the table. Defaults to 0. |

## Description

Opens the window, or full screen mode, that 3D programs are drawn in. It has to be the first graphics command of a 3D program: every other 3D command fails until it ran. After it, the back buffer is the target of drawing and you draw one frame at a time with [RenderWorld](RenderWorld) and [Flip](Flip).

| Mode | Behavior |
|---|---|
| 0 | Window while testing and full screen otherwise. This is the default. |
| 1 | Full screen. |
| 2 | Window. |
| 3 | Window whose size can be changed by the user; the picture is scaled to fit. |
| 4 | Window without a border: no title bar and no frame. This is a BlitzLLVM extension that original Blitz does not have. |

## Differences

* The depth does not pick a video mode, it picks the format of the buffers: 24 is R8G8B8X8, 30 is R10G10B10A2, 32 is R8G8B8A8 and 64 is R16G16B16A16 with half precision floats. 0, 16 and any other number give 32 (with a warning for the others), and a format that the graphics card can't draw to gives the next smaller one. Pixels are read and written as 8 bits per channel whatever the depth is. See [Color depth](Color-Depth).
* Full screen (mode 1) does not change the video mode of the display: the picture is shown at the largest size that fits with its aspect ratio kept, and the rest is black. See [Fullscreen](Fullscreen).
* A window without a border (mode 4) has the size you ask for and cannot be resized by the user.

## Examples

```blitzbasic
Graphics3D 640, 480, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
camera = CreateCamera()
cube = CreateCube()
PositionEntity cube, 0, 0, 5

While Not KeyHit(1)
	TurnEntity cube, 1, 2, 0
	RenderWorld
	Flip
Wend
```
